title: 50 Things You NEED to Know About GTA 6 (Before You Play)
note: status: confirmed = Rockstar or several independent outlets; reported = one preview/interview as reported by outlets (said aloud as 'according to ...' or 'from the previews'); conflicting = sources disagree (said aloud).

sections.text: GTA 6 is finally out, it's sitting at a ninety-nine on Metacritic, and most people are about to play it exactly like GTA 5. That's a mistake. In GTA 6, the cash in your pocket can disappear, the cops vanish from your mini map, and some story missions won't even start until you've earned the money yourself. So here are fifty things you need to know about GTA 6, the stuff the game won't tell you. Stay for number fifty, because it changes the whole story. Quick note: when something comes from a preview or an interview, I'll say so. Nothing here is made up.

sections.label: BEFORE YOU PRESS START
sections.text: Let's start with the stuff you need to know before you even press start.

sections.label: CONSOLES ONLY
sections.text: Number one. GTA 6 is out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. That's it. There's no PC version yet, and Rockstar hasn't given one a date.

sections.label: CLEAR YOUR STORAGE
sections.text: Number two. Clear some space. The install is reported at around two hundred and ten gigabytes, depending on your console. So delete whatever you're not playing.

sections.label: 30 FPS EVERYWHERE
sections.text: Number three. Rockstar confirmed GTA 6 targets thirty frames per second on every console, PS5 Pro included. The Pro gets a sharper image and ray traced shadows, but not a sixty F P S mode at launch.

sections.label: A 99 ON METACRITIC
sections.text: Number four. The reviews are in, and GTA 6 launched with a ninety-nine on Metacritic. That ties The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the highest score ever.

sections.label: NO ONLINE YET
sections.text: Number five. There's no GTA 6 Online at launch, and no release date for it. Reports point to sometime in twenty twenty-seven, and your GTA 5 Online character is not coming with you.

sections.label: NO FIRST PERSON
sections.text: Number six. Don't look for a first person mode. Rob Nelson from Rockstar North said there isn't a full one. You only get first person when you aim with certain weapons.
sources: Rob Nelson interview with Davy Jones via VICE

sections.label: WELCOME TO LEONIDA
sections.text: Now, the world itself, because it's not just Vice City.

sections.label: SIX REGIONS
sections.text: Number seven. The whole game takes place in Leonida, Rockstar's version of Florida. There's Vice City, the Leonida Keys, the Grassrivers swamps, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park.
sources: Rockstar official media kit (screenshot folders by place)

sections.label: TWICE GTA 5
sections.text: Number eight. How big is it? Rob Nelson told the YouTuber T G G the map is about twice the size of GTA 5, and around three times Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar hasn't given an exact number, so any square kilometre figure you see online is a fan estimate.
sources: Rob Nelson to TGG via Rockstar Intel/TechSpot

sections.label: YOU START IN THE KEYS
sections.text: Number nine. You don't start in Vice City. According to Rob Nelson, the opening is down in the Leonida Keys, where Jason is living. So don't panic if you're stuck on a small island at first. The state opens up after that.
sources: Rob Nelson (Famitsu/IGN) as reported by Hollywood GTA

sections.label: THE MAP IS HIDDEN
sections.text: Number ten. The map starts hidden. Places you haven't visited stay covered until you actually go there, like the fog of war in Red Dead 2. And a lot of what's out there isn't marked at all.
sources: Famitsu via gameranx and Hollywood GTA

sections.label: HUNDREDS OF INTERIORS
sections.text: Number eleven. You can walk into way more buildings. Rob Nelson used the word hundreds when he talked about interiors, and a lot of them tie into the new robbery system.

sections.label: 170+ ANIMALS
sections.text: Number twelve. Leonida has more than one hundred and seventy animal species, on land, in the air and in the water. And some of them are rare or even legendary, which Rockstar hasn't revealed yet.

sections.label: LOCAL WEATHER
sections.text: Number thirteen. The weather is local now. It can be sunny where you are while a storm hits another part of the map. And yes, there are tropical storms and hurricanes.

sections.label: 600,000 ANIMATIONS
sections.text: Number fourteen. The people in Leonida feel alive for a reason. Rockstar says there are over six hundred thousand animations in GTA 6. GTA 5 had about fifty-five thousand.

sections.label: ~80 HOURS
sections.text: Number fifteen. Don't rush it. Rob Nelson told the New York Times his own playthrough took about eighty hours, including some optional goals. That's one person's run, not a promise, but it would make this Rockstar's longest story yet.

sections.label: JASON & LUCIA
sections.text: Next, the two people you're actually playing as.

sections.label: SWITCH ANYTIME (MOSTLY)
sections.text: Number sixteen. Outside of missions you can switch between Jason and Lucia when the story lets you. But some missions are locked to one of them, so if you can't switch, that's not a bug.
sources: Rob Nelson via IGN, as reported by Hollywood GTA and gameranx

sections.label: THEY HAVE LIVES
sections.text: Number seventeen. The one you're not playing doesn't freeze in place. According to Nelson, they get their own routine and go off and do their own thing.

sections.label: PASS THE WHEEL
sections.text: Number eighteen. When you're both in a car, you can let your partner drive and jump to the passenger seat to shoot. In a cop chase, that changes everything.

sections.label: THE RELATIONSHIP
sections.text: Number nineteen. Their relationship is a real system, and it's optional. You build it by spending time together, like the gym, the beach, or a job. Previews disagree on whether there's a visible meter, but Rockstar says it shapes how their story plays out.

sections.label: THE GYM IS BACK
sections.text: Number twenty. The gym is back. Cardio builds stamina, lifting builds health, and your character's body actually changes. You'll need a membership to get in.

sections.label: FOOD = BUFFS
sections.text: Number twenty-one. Food is a boost, not a chore. Coffee for stamina, bigger meals for health. But eat way too much and, yes, you'll gain weight.

sections.label: MONEY
sections.text: Now money, because this is where GTA 5 habits will burn you.

sections.label: 3 KINDS OF MONEY
sections.text: Number twenty-two. Your money comes in three forms: what's in the bank, the cash on you, and stolen goods you still have to sell.

sections.label: DIE = LOSE YOUR CASH
sections.text: Number twenty-three. Get killed or busted, and every dollar you're carrying is gone. Rob Nelson confirmed it. So before you do anything stupid, find an ATM and bank your cash.

sections.label: MISSIONS COST MONEY
sections.text: Number twenty-four. Some story missions won't start until you've raised money yourself. In Nelson's words to Famitsu, just completing missions won't give you enough money to progress the story.

sections.label: FIND A FENCE
sections.text: Number twenty-five. Stolen goods aren't money yet. You sell them to a fence, and each fence only buys certain things, like cars or jewelry. Keep the good ones close, because they start giving you work.

sections.label: YOUR FIRST ROBBERY
sections.text: And you're going to make most of that money the fun way.

sections.label: ROB (ALMOST) ANY STORE
sections.text: Number twenty-six. You can rob a lot of the stores you walk into, not just the marked ones. The small ones don't show up on your map, so you find them by driving around.

sections.label: LOUD OR QUIET
sections.text: Number twenty-seven. Kick the door in and the alarm goes off. Or go quiet: sneak in the back, deal with the cameras and the alarm, and you're gone before anyone calls it in.

sections.label: THEY FIGHT BACK
sections.text: Number twenty-eight. Floridians fight back. Clerks, security and even customers can turn on you, so look at who's inside before you pull a gun.

sections.label: THE SAFE
sections.text: Number twenty-nine. The register is quick money, the safe is the real payday. Blow it open and it's fast but you damage some of the loot. Find the code and you get all of it, if you have the time.

sections.label: BIGGER JOBS
sections.text: Number thirty. Jewelry stores and small banks are on the table too, but the police response is a lot heavier. Don't make a bank your first job.

sections.label: THE COPS
sections.text: Halfway there. And this next part is the biggest change in the whole game: the cops.

sections.label: NO WITNESS, NO CRIME
sections.text: Number thirty-one. A crime only gets reported if somebody sees it, or an alarm goes off. No witness, no call.

sections.label: SIX STARS ARE BACK
sections.text: Number thirty-two. The wanted level goes up to six stars again. GTA 5 was the only 3D GTA that stopped at five.

sections.label: NO COPS ON THE RADAR
sections.text: Number thirty-three. Once they're on you, police no longer show up as dots on your mini map. You get a search area instead, so you actually have to look.

sections.label: WHAT THEY KNOW
sections.text: Number thirty-four. Next to your stars there are icons for what the police know: your face, your outfit, your car, your weapon, whether you're a pair, even whether a camera caught you.

sections.label: HOW TO SHAKE THEM
sections.text: Number thirty-five. Every icon has a fix. They know your outfit? Change it, completely. Your car? Swap it. Looking for two people? Split Jason and Lucia up.
sources: Edge preview as reported by gameranx/Hollywood GTA

sections.label: HOLLOW STARS
sections.text: Number thirty-six. If your stars show up hollow, the cops know something happened but they don't know it was you. Don't run, don't shoot. Just walk away.
sources: previews as reported by gameranx and Hollywood GTA

sections.label: K-9 UNITS
sections.text: Number thirty-seven. The police brought new toys: dogs, spike strips, and helicopters with searchlights. In Edge's preview, a police dog took Jason down after a failed robbery.

sections.label: CRIMINAL PROFILE
sections.text: Number thirty-eight. The game tracks what kind of criminal you are, from professional all the way to irredeemable. Do the job clean and you stay professional. Go overboard, and it follows you.

sections.label: CARS
sections.text: Now cars, because stealing one isn't one button anymore.

sections.label: NOT ONE BUTTON
sections.text: Number thirty-nine. Older cars you can break into and hotwire. Newer ones have real security, and the best cars need tools you only get later in the story. So don't waste night one on a parked supercar.

sections.label: SCAN BEFORE YOU STEAL
sections.text: Number forty. There's a phone app called WAINK. Point it at a car and it tells you if it's locked, alarmed, tracked, and what it's worth.

sections.label: TRACKERS
sections.text: Number forty-one. Watch out for trackers. Reportedly, some of them alert the cops if you drive too slowly, so keep your foot down.

sections.label: FILL UP
sections.text: Number forty-two. Cars run on gas now. Filling up only takes a few seconds, but it's reported that Rob Nelson himself ran out of fuel during a police chase in a demo.

sections.label: MAKE IT YOURS
sections.text: Number forty-three. Want to keep a stolen car? You'll have to register it in your name, and pricier cars cost more. Garage space is limited too, so keep the ones you love.

sections.label: GUNS & LIFE
sections.text: Last stretch: guns, and everything that isn't crime.

sections.label: NO MORE POCKET ARSENAL
sections.text: Number forty-four. You can't carry an army in your pocket anymore. It's two concealed handguns and two long guns, one on your back and one in your hands. The rest lives in your car's trunk.

sections.label: THE WHEEL SURVIVED
sections.text: Number forty-five. A fun one. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier says Rockstar spent months, maybe years, trying to replace the weapon wheel. In the end, the wheel won.

sections.label: PEOPLE NOTICE
sections.text: Number forty-six. People react to you. Walk down the street with a rifle out and they will notice, back off, or even call it in.

sections.label: FOCUS MODE
sections.text: Number forty-seven. Learn focus. It slows time and shows weak spots, and in the previews, a yellow marker meant you could take someone down without killing them. That's how you stay professional.

sections.label: RADIO ON FOOT
sections.text: Number forty-eight. For the first time, you can listen to the radio and podcasts on foot with headphones. Bad Bunny co-hosts Cocoteo FM, Flash FM is back from Vice City, and two members of Slayer run the metal station.

sections.label: SO MUCH TO DO
sections.text: Number forty-nine. When you need a break: pool, mini golf, kayaking, fishing, hunting, scuba diving, and that's not even the full list.

sections.label: YOUR STORY CHANGES
sections.text: And number fifty. The story you get depends on how you play. Rob Nelson's eighty hours included optional goals with narrative ramifications, and your criminal profile and Jason and Lucia's relationship both feed into how it plays out. Two people can finish GTA 6 with a different experience.
sources: New York Times via GamesRadar ('optional goals with narrative ramifications')

sections.text: That's fifty things you need to know about GTA 6. Which one surprised you the most? Tell me in the comments. And if this helped, subscribe, because this channel is all GTA 6, and there's a lot more coming. See you in Leonida.
